column4: This car just drove upside down.
And the crazy part? It barely needs any speed to do it.
Imagine you're driving it, on Halloween night.
You floor it. Tesla claims zero to sixty in under a second.
That's almost three G's. About double what astronauts feel at liftoff.
No tire can grip that hard. So it cheats, with thrusters.
Cold gas blasts out the back, like letting go of a balloon.
But the ghost is gaining. So you aim for the ramp.
On a curve, the car wants to fly straight. So it presses into the track.
Even upside down. At the top of a small loop, twenty miles an hour is enough.
In 2012, stunt drivers looped two real cars at once.
So why the thrusters? To launch. Flip. And fly.
Tesla says it ships in 2028. It's missed dates before. Would you ride it?
